Severe Flooding Disrupts UAE Oil & Gas Services and Equipment Operations

Oil and gas services and equipment providers in the United Arab Emirates are grappling with widespread operational disruptions as severe flooding, triggered by days of torrential rainfall, inundates key industrial sites and transport routes. The ongoing event, which began on Monday, has affected critical infrastructure in Abu Dhabi’s Al Ruwais industrial area and several logistics corridors serving the sector.

According to the UAE Oilfield Services Association, at least six major service yards and storage facilities in the Al Ruwais zone are partially submerged, forcing the suspension of equipment maintenance and dispatch activities. “This is the most significant weather-related disruption we have seen in over a decade,” said Faisal Al Mansouri, the association’s spokesperson. “Many operators are unable to access their sites, and vital equipment is at risk of water damage.”

Floodwaters have also rendered sections of the E11 and E15 highways impassable, delaying the movement of drilling rigs, pressure pumping units, and other large-scale equipment to both onshore and offshore projects. The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure confirmed that emergency crews are working around the clock to clear debris and restore road access, but warned that persistent rainfall is hampering progress.

Al Waha Petroleum Services, which operates a major equipment yard near the affected industrial zone, reported that up to 40% of its fleet is currently immobilized. “We are monitoring the situation closely and have shifted focus to safeguarding high-value assets,” said Mohsin Al Jaberi, operations director at Al Waha. “Our immediate concern is to prevent long-term damage to electronic systems and hydraulic assemblies.”

Industry analysts caution that the flooding could have knock-on effects on drilling schedules and maintenance cycles for ongoing projects in the Western Region and offshore fields. “Any prolonged interruption in the supply of critical equipment or technical services can cause significant project delays, especially for time-sensitive operations,” said Lina Rahman, an independent sector analyst based in Dubai.

In response, several companies have activated business continuity plans, including the temporary relocation of staff and equipment to higher ground. The UAE Oilfield Workers’ Union has called for enhanced safety measures, urging all employers to prioritize worker safety and ensure adequate shelter and emergency provisions at all impacted sites.

With meteorological authorities forecasting further rain through the coming week, the industry faces ongoing uncertainty. “We urge all service providers and contractors to remain vigilant and to cooperate fully with civil defense teams,” said Al Mansouri. “The priority now is to protect lives, assets, and to restore critical operations as soon as conditions allow.”

The situation remains fluid, with the full extent of operational and material losses yet to be determined.
